t: A Viking settlement on the lower Seine, granted to Rollo in 911, that became a French duchy ruled from Rouen.
Its dukes kept unusually firm control over castles, barons and the Church, and its abbeys such as Bec led European learning.
Duke William conquered England in 1066; Philip II of France annexed the duchy in 1204.
dyk: The Channel Islands are the last part of the old Duchy of Normandy still held by the British crown, and their law still rests partly on Norman custom.
ev: Charles the Simple grants the Viking leader Rollo lands around Rouen
Herluin founds the abbey of Bec, later home to Lanfranc and Anselm
William II defeats rebel barons at the Battle of Val-ès-Dunes
Duke William defeats Harold Godwinson at Hastings and becomes King of England
Henry I of England defeats Robert Curthose at the Battle of Tinchebray
Geoffrey Plantagenet takes Rouen and is recognised as duke
Philip II of France takes Château Gaillard and Rouen and annexes Normandy

f.capital: Rouen; Caen also a major ducal centre
